payload.title: Test the reported pro-female evaluation bias in Jev at scale
payload.description: A public write-up (urasmutlu.dev, 'A First Look at Jev', September 2026) scored 34 hand-written male/female/they scenario triples on competence, likability and hireability with Jev's score primitive and found the female variant scored higher on 33 of 34 pairs (mean absolute delta 0.155 on a 0-4 scale), largest on assertive and emotional scenarios (e.g. pounding the table, -0.46 hireability). Our gendered-language pre-registration (2a384ef) predicts the opposite for loaded words. Test it on real bios at n = 2,000 with a floor: evaluative questions (competence, likability, promotability) alongside our occupation-assignment questions, pronoun and name cues, the singular-they variant as a third arm (it is itself a cue, not a neutral baseline), and the ask-twice noise floor. Report both directions: a boost for women on evaluation and a push toward lower-status roles on assignment can coexist.
